hero.headline: Vero Beach shooting victim identified as Dawn Kriskewic, suspect Matthew Waggle remains at large
hero.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. The Sheriff's Office announced the identif
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. The Sheriff's Office announced the identification on Tuesday after locating and notifying several out-of-state next of kin. The victim's body was found in a roadway at 501 First Street in Vero Beach on Sunday at 8:41 a.m.

Deputies found Kriskewic with an apparent gunshot wound and began life-saving measures. She was transported to a local hospital where she was pronounced dead. Detectives and crime scene personnel processed the scene outside the victim's home. The Sheriff's Office is treating the case as a domestic violence homicide.

The Sheriff's Office named 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle of Sebastian as a person of interest. Sheriff Eric Flowers said Kriskewic and Waggle were in some sort of relationship. Investigators believe the victim had been trying to end the relationship with Waggle. A nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle, who authorities believe has left Indian River County and is traveling by vehicle.

Sheriff Flowers warned that Waggle should be considered armed and dangerous and should not be approached. Investigators are using resources including flock cameras and the Real Time Crime Center to search for Waggle. As of Tuesday afternoon, law enforcement continues its investigation and search. Anyone with information about the case or Waggle's whereabouts is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or submit information anonymously to Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds wins Republican nomination for Florida governor, David Jolly takes Democratic nod
cards.teaser: Byron Donalds won the Republican nomination for Florida governor on Tuesday, defeating opponents including former Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins and political .
cards.body:
Byron Donalds won the Republican nomination for Florida governor on Tuesday, defeating opponents including former Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins and political newcomer James Fishback. Former U.S. Representative David Jolly captured the Democratic nomination, setting the stage for a November contest to replace outgoing Governor Ron DeSantis, who is barred from running for a third consecutive term.

Donalds, 47, triumphed with backing from President Trump and promises to push tax cuts, overhaul Florida's insurance regulations to lower consumer costs and seek greater price transparency from healthcare providers. There have been three elected Black governors in U.S. history, and Donalds could become Florida's first. Jolly, 53, is a former Republican U.S. representative who became a fierce critic of Trump, turned independent, and joined the Democratic Party last year. For the second time in a row, Florida Democrats have chosen a former Republican as their candidate for governor. Four years ago, Democrats backed former Republican Governor Charlie Crist, who was easily defeated by DeSantis by nearly 20 percentage points.

Trump has had an inconsistent record on picks for governor in primaries this year, and a strong showing by Donalds would leave Republicans in a more commanding position for November. Though DeSantis coasted to reelection in 2022, he squeaked into office in 2018 by little more than 32,000 ballots out of 8.1 million cast. Rich Chamberlin, a retiree in Port St. Lucie, said he supported Jolly in Tuesday's primary, spurred on by attack ads against him. Chamberlin said he saw anti-Jolly ads and decided if they were against him, then he must be for him, adding it did not matter to him that Jolly was once a Republican.

Tuesday's primaries gave final form to a November ballot whose races will test Trump's grip on his adopted state and Democrats' ability to resurrect Florida as a national political battleground. Florida has moved notably to the right since Trump won his first election in 2016, though Democrats hope to regain ground from his slumping popularity ratings. DeSantis, a leading conservative figure who has clashed and collaborated with Trump over the years, praised Donalds as ready to continue conservative policies in the state.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie mayoral candidates debate growth, traffic, and infrastructure ahead of Election Day
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie voters are deciding Tuesday who will lead the city, with incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin facing challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri in a race focused on gr
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie voters are deciding Tuesday who will lead the city, with incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin facing challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri in a race focused on growth, traffic, development and infrastructure. The mayoral race is nonpartisan, and polls close Tuesday at 7 p.m. If one candidate receives more than 50% of the vote, that candidate wins outright. If no candidate reaches 50%, the top two vote-getters advance to the November general election.

The candidates offered different approaches to managing growth in one of Florida's largest cities. Giordano said he wants to slow down development and ensure existing infrastructure can handle what is already being built, focusing on drainage systems, roads and traffic infrastructure. Martin said many development rights were granted more than 20 years ago and cannot simply be taken away by the current City Council, but pointed to Rosser Lakes Preserve as an example where the city prevented a developer from building 86 homes and instead acquired the land as green space. Port St. Lucie has acquired more than 280 acres of green space since January 2025. Strazzeri said he supports responsible growth but believes roads, schools, utilities and emergency services need to be in place before communities are developed.

All three candidates acknowledged traffic as a major issue. Giordano called traffic in St. Lucie West a nightmare and said it takes almost 30 minutes to get from one end to the other, which he called totally unacceptable. He wants a new traffic study examining roadways, traffic signals and signal timing. Martin pointed to projects already underway, including work on Floresta Drive and Port St. Lucie Boulevard South, roundabouts in Torino and planned intersection improvements at Tradition Parkway and Village Parkway, Savona Boulevard and Gatlin Boulevard. Strazzeri said the city needs to be proactive and not reactive, calling for better traffic signal coordination, adaptive signal technology and road expansion where possible.

Martin has served as Port St. Lucie's mayor for the past five years and previously served on the City Council starting in 2010. She said the city has lowered its property tax rate each year for the past 11 years, reducing the rate by 25% over that period. Giordano said he has lived in Port St. Lucie since 1989 and has nearly 20 years of public service experience, including about a decade with the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Strazzeri said he moved to Port St. Lucie in 2015, served in the Army and deployed to Iraq as a combat engineer, and later transitioned into information technology and cybersecurity.

cards.headline: Christopher 'Doc' Collins wins Martin County Commission District 2 seat
cards.teaser: Christopher 'Doc' Collins won the open Martin County Commission District 2 seat Tuesday, defeating Susan O'Rourke and Althea Wiley in a Universal Primary Contest that decided the r
cards.body:
Christopher 'Doc' Collins won the open Martin County Commission District 2 seat Tuesday, defeating Susan O'Rourke and Althea Wiley in a Universal Primary Contest that decided the race outright. Collins received 14,657 votes, or about 49 percent, while O'Rourke received 12,065 votes, about 40 percent, and Wiley received 3,194 votes, nearly 11 percent. Because all three candidates were Republicans and no Democrat qualified, Tuesday's vote decided the seat with no November general election to follow.

Collins, a chiropractor and former Stuart city commissioner and mayor, stepped down from the Stuart City Commission earlier this year to run for the county seat, a move required under the city's charter before he could qualify for another elected office. He ran largely on a platform of slow growth, calling for tighter restrictions on new development across the county. During his time on the Stuart City Commission, Collins joined two other commissioners in voting to rescind the city's agreement with Brightline for a downtown train station, a position that put him at odds with O'Rourke throughout the campaign.

The campaign had a tense moment in its final week, when Collins accused a man named Jim Gallegos of stealing his campaign signs, posting a Facebook video with trail camera footage and Apple AirTag tracking he said showed Gallegos pulling one of his signs from the ground. Gallegos denied stealing anything, saying he removed roughly 30 signs for various candidates, including some of Collins', at a property owner's request. The dispute also drew in Derreck Ogden, a Stuart City Commission candidate, who publicly confronted Gallegos over the signs.

Collins will replace outgoing Commissioner Stacey Hetherington, who chose not to seek re election. O'Rourke, a former traffic engineer who previously served on Stuart's Local Planning Agency, ran on managing growth and easing traffic congestion. Her candidacy became the subject of a legal dispute earlier this year after Collins filed a challenge seeking to have her removed from the ballot, arguing she was not legally a Martin County resident when she qualified. A judge dismissed that challenge in July. Wiley, an author, Realtor and chef, ran on affordability, pointing to rising housing costs and other everyday expenses facing county residents.

cards.headline: Former Vero Beach Eagles secretary accused of spending $419,000 on guns, liquor, LEGOs
cards.teaser: Robert John Davison allegedly used nearly $419,000 of Fraternal Order of Eagles funds for personal expenses including firearms, DUI fees, and items for his personal LEGO business.
cards.body:
Robert John Davison, who served as secretary of Aerie 4374 Fraternal Order of Eagles in Vero Beach from February 2015 until November 2024, allegedly spent nearly $419,000 of the organization's money on personal purchases. The investigation began after a representative from the Grand Aerie examined why membership and finances were declining at the chapter. The representative discovered that Davison had been using the organization's debit card for unauthorized personal purchases.

The organization hired forensic accounting firm Clay Price & Associates, P.A. to review financial records. On February 24, 2025, the firm reported that Davison had used $418,899.26 in organization funds for personal expenses dating back to 2017. The alleged spending included $8,791.14 on firearms, ammunition, personal purchases and an NRA membership, $35,094.53 in personal grocery and liquor store purchases, and at least $2,461.37 in purchases for Davison's personal LEGO business.

Other alleged expenses included $4,463.52 in personal court payments including child support and DUI-related fees, $55,175.40 on personal bills including credit cards and vehicle payments, $115,087.49 in ATM withdrawals and associated fees, $9,861.27 in transfers to Davison's personal Cash App account, $16,038.66 in unauthorized flights and lodging, $5,930.98 in rideshare expenses, and $2,476.43 in personal fuel purchases. Davison is accused of embezzlement involving a value of $100,000 or more.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County voters respond to arrest of Clerk and Comptroller Mike Caruso on primary election day
cards.teaser: Voters in Palm Beach County headed to the polls Tuesday amid a major shake-up after Republican candidate Mike Caruso was arrested and is being held without bond.
cards.body:
Mike Caruso served seven years in the Florida House, representing parts of Palm Beach County, before Governor Ron DeSantis appointed him as Palm Beach County Clerk and Comptroller in August of last year. His arrest came on primary election day. Although his name is not on the ballot as he is running uncontested, his removal from the race leaves Republicans without a candidate for the seat.

One voter called the development pretty shocking because Caruso is the Clerk of Court, saying people in that position should hold themselves to a higher level of standard. Another voter expressed frustration over losing their candidate, saying it sucks when a candidate drops off the map like that and expressing hope the Republican Party would be able to do some kind of referendum, while noting dislike for appointed candidates. Voters said the controversy should not keep people from participating and coming out to vote, and that their voices still matter at the polls.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.teaser: Voters in Palm Beach County headed to the polls Tuesday amid a major shake-up after Republican candidate Mike Caruso was arrested and is being held without bond.
hero.body:
Mike Caruso served seven years in the Florida House, representing parts of Palm Beach County, before Governor Ron DeSantis appointed him as Palm Beach County Clerk and Comptroller in August of last year. His arrest came on primary election day. Although his name is not on the ballot as he is running uncontested, his removal from the race leaves Republicans without a candidate for the seat.

One voter called the development pretty shocking because Caruso is the Clerk of Court, saying people in that position should hold themselves to a higher level of standard. Another voter expressed frustration over losing their candidate, saying it sucks when a candidate drops off the map like that and expressing hope the Republican Party would be able to do some kind of referendum, while noting dislike for appointed candidates. Voters said the controversy should not keep people from participating and coming out to vote, and that their voices still matter at the polls.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds wins Republican nomination for Florida governor, David Jolly takes Democratic nod
cards.teaser: Byron Donalds won the Republican nomination for Florida governor on Tuesday, defeating opponents including former Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins and political .
cards.body:
Byron Donalds won the Republican nomination for Florida governor on Tuesday, defeating opponents including former Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins and political newcomer James Fishback. Former U.S. Representative David Jolly captured the Democratic nomination, setting the stage for a November contest to replace outgoing Governor Ron DeSantis, who is barred from running for a third consecutive term.

Donalds, 47, triumphed with backing from President Trump and promises to push tax cuts, overhaul Florida's insurance regulations to lower consumer costs and seek greater price transparency from healthcare providers. There have been three elected Black governors in U.S. history, and Donalds could become Florida's first. Jolly, 53, is a former Republican U.S. representative who became a fierce critic of Trump, turned independent, and joined the Democratic Party last year. For the second time in a row, Florida Democrats have chosen a former Republican as their candidate for governor. Four years ago, Democrats backed former Republican Governor Charlie Crist, who was easily defeated by DeSantis by nearly 20 percentage points.

Trump has had an inconsistent record on picks for governor in primaries this year, and a strong showing by Donalds would leave Republicans in a more commanding position for November. Though DeSantis coasted to reelection in 2022, he squeaked into office in 2018 by little more than 32,000 ballots out of 8.1 million cast. Rich Chamberlin, a retiree in Port St. Lucie, said he supported Jolly in Tuesday's primary, spurred on by attack ads against him. Chamberlin said he saw anti-Jolly ads and decided if they were against him, then he must be for him, adding it did not matter to him that Jolly was once a Republican.

Tuesday's primaries gave final form to a November ballot whose races will test Trump's grip on his adopted state and Democrats' ability to resurrect Florida as a national political battleground. Florida has moved notably to the right since Trump won his first election in 2016, though Democrats hope to regain ground from his slumping popularity ratings. DeSantis, a leading conservative figure who has clashed and collaborated with Trump over the years, praised Donalds as ready to continue conservative policies in the state.

hero.headline: Christopher 'Doc' Collins wins Martin County Commission District 2 seat
hero.teaser: Christopher 'Doc' Collins won the open Martin County Commission District 2 seat Tuesday, defeating Susan O'Rourke and Althea Wiley in a Universal Primary Contest that decided the r
hero.body:
Christopher 'Doc' Collins won the open Martin County Commission District 2 seat Tuesday, defeating Susan O'Rourke and Althea Wiley in a Universal Primary Contest that decided the race outright. Collins received 14,657 votes, or about 49 percent, while O'Rourke received 12,065 votes, about 40 percent, and Wiley received 3,194 votes, nearly 11 percent. Because all three candidates were Republicans and no Democrat qualified, Tuesday's vote decided the seat with no November general election to follow.

Collins, a chiropractor and former Stuart city commissioner and mayor, stepped down from the Stuart City Commission earlier this year to run for the county seat, a move required under the city's charter before he could qualify for another elected office. He ran largely on a platform of slow growth, calling for tighter restrictions on new development across the county. During his time on the Stuart City Commission, Collins joined two other commissioners in voting to rescind the city's agreement with Brightline for a downtown train station, a position that put him at odds with O'Rourke throughout the campaign.

The campaign had a tense moment in its final week, when Collins accused a man named Jim Gallegos of stealing his campaign signs, posting a Facebook video with trail camera footage and Apple AirTag tracking he said showed Gallegos pulling one of his signs from the ground. Gallegos denied stealing anything, saying he removed roughly 30 signs for various candidates, including some of Collins', at a property owner's request. The dispute also drew in Derreck Ogden, a Stuart City Commission candidate, who publicly confronted Gallegos over the signs.

Collins will replace outgoing Commissioner Stacey Hetherington, who chose not to seek re election. O'Rourke, a former traffic engineer who previously served on Stuart's Local Planning Agency, ran on managing growth and easing traffic congestion. Her candidacy became the subject of a legal dispute earlier this year after Collins filed a challenge seeking to have her removed from the ballot, arguing she was not legally a Martin County resident when she qualified. A judge dismissed that challenge in July. Wiley, an author, Realtor and chef, ran on affordability, pointing to rising housing costs and other everyday expenses facing county residents.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie mayoral candidates debate growth, traffic, and infrastructure ahead of Election Day
hero.teaser: Port St. Lucie voters are deciding Tuesday who will lead the city, with incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin facing challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri in a race focused on gr
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie voters are deciding Tuesday who will lead the city, with incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin facing challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri in a race focused on growth, traffic, development and infrastructure. The mayoral race is nonpartisan, and polls close Tuesday at 7 p.m. If one candidate receives more than 50% of the vote, that candidate wins outright. If no candidate reaches 50%, the top two vote-getters advance to the November general election.

The candidates offered different approaches to managing growth in one of Florida's largest cities. Giordano said he wants to slow down development and ensure existing infrastructure can handle what is already being built, focusing on drainage systems, roads and traffic infrastructure. Martin said many development rights were granted more than 20 years ago and cannot simply be taken away by the current City Council, but pointed to Rosser Lakes Preserve as an example where the city prevented a developer from building 86 homes and instead acquired the land as green space. Port St. Lucie has acquired more than 280 acres of green space since January 2025. Strazzeri said he supports responsible growth but believes roads, schools, utilities and emergency services need to be in place before communities are developed.

All three candidates acknowledged traffic as a major issue. Giordano called traffic in St. Lucie West a nightmare and said it takes almost 30 minutes to get from one end to the other, which he called totally unacceptable. He wants a new traffic study examining roadways, traffic signals and signal timing. Martin pointed to projects already underway, including work on Floresta Drive and Port St. Lucie Boulevard South, roundabouts in Torino and planned intersection improvements at Tradition Parkway and Village Parkway, Savona Boulevard and Gatlin Boulevard. Strazzeri said the city needs to be proactive and not reactive, calling for better traffic signal coordination, adaptive signal technology and road expansion where possible.

Martin has served as Port St. Lucie's mayor for the past five years and previously served on the City Council starting in 2010. She said the city has lowered its property tax rate each year for the past 11 years, reducing the rate by 25% over that period. Giordano said he has lived in Port St. Lucie since 1989 and has nearly 20 years of public service experience, including about a decade with the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Strazzeri said he moved to Port St. Lucie in 2015, served in the Army and deployed to Iraq as a combat engineer, and later transitioned into information technology and cybersecurity.

hero.headline: Vero Beach shooting victim identified as Dawn Kriskewic, suspect Matthew Waggle remains at large
hero.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. The Sheriff's Office announced the identif
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. The Sheriff's Office announced the identification on Tuesday after locating and notifying several out-of-state next of kin. The victim's body was found in a roadway at 501 First Street in Vero Beach on Sunday at 8:41 a.m.

Deputies found Kriskewic with an apparent gunshot wound and began life-saving measures. She was transported to a local hospital where she was pronounced dead. Detectives and crime scene personnel processed the scene outside the victim's home. The Sheriff's Office is treating the case as a domestic violence homicide.

The Sheriff's Office named 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle of Sebastian as a person of interest. Sheriff Eric Flowers said Kriskewic and Waggle were in some sort of relationship. Investigators believe the victim had been trying to end the relationship with Waggle. A nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle, who authorities believe has left Indian River County and is traveling by vehicle.

Sheriff Flowers warned that Waggle should be considered armed and dangerous and should not be approached. Investigators are using resources including flock cameras and the Real Time Crime Center to search for Waggle. As of Tuesday afternoon, law enforcement continues its investigation and search. Anyone with information about the case or Waggle's whereabouts is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or submit information anonymously to Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Former Vero Beach Eagles secretary accused of spending $419,000 on guns, liquor, LEGOs
cards.teaser: Robert John Davison allegedly used nearly $419,000 of Fraternal Order of Eagles funds for personal expenses including firearms, DUI fees, and items for his personal LEGO business.
cards.body:
Robert John Davison, who served as secretary of Aerie 4374 Fraternal Order of Eagles in Vero Beach from February 2015 until November 2024, allegedly spent nearly $419,000 of the organization's money on personal purchases. The investigation began after a representative from the Grand Aerie examined why membership and finances were declining at the chapter. The representative discovered that Davison had been using the organization's debit card for unauthorized personal purchases.

The organization hired forensic accounting firm Clay Price & Associates, P.A. to review financial records. On February 24, 2025, the firm reported that Davison had used $418,899.26 in organization funds for personal expenses dating back to 2017. The alleged spending included $8,791.14 on firearms, ammunition, personal purchases and an NRA membership, $35,094.53 in personal grocery and liquor store purchases, and at least $2,461.37 in purchases for Davison's personal LEGO business.

Other alleged expenses included $4,463.52 in personal court payments including child support and DUI-related fees, $55,175.40 on personal bills including credit cards and vehicle payments, $115,087.49 in ATM withdrawals and associated fees, $9,861.27 in transfers to Davison's personal Cash App account, $16,038.66 in unauthorized flights and lodging, $5,930.98 in rideshare expenses, and $2,476.43 in personal fuel purchases. Davison is accused of embezzlement involving a value of $100,000 or more.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.
